messages.subject: multicolour histograms on density scale
parts:
Hi all,

I've sent this message, but due to an unreliable internet connection I
am unsure if it really made it through. Apologies if there will be
multiple posts.


I have a question regarding multicolour histograms (barplots) on
"density scale".

The background:
I want to plot the histogram of vector X. And I want to fit a
distribution using only some portion of X. This fit should be
overlayed.

Additionally, the part of the histogram used in the distribution
fitting should be coloured.

Here is an example:
#+begin_src R
X <- rnorm(100)
idx <- (abs(X) < 0.5)

library("fitdistrplus")

centerfit <- fitdist(X[idx], "norm")


plot_df <- data.frame(X=X, used=idx)

ggplot(plot_df, aes(x=X)) +
geom_histogram(aes(y = ..density.., fill=idx)) +
stat_function(geom="line",
fun=dnorm,
arg=list(mean=centerfit$estimate["mean"],
sd=centerfit$estimate["sd"]),
colour="darkred")
#+end_src

This works fine, except for the "wrong" scaling of the part of the
histogram not used in the fitting. Both coloured regions seem to be
scaled separately. How can I avoid that?

Many thanks in advance,
Andreas
